advisories.title: view.schemaDigests: deliberate selection or required union of fact/coverage payload schemas?
advisories.severityBasis: A published normative sentence and a field annotation are unenforced by the accepted closure, and the drift is already present in a committed record in the live tree.

actualObservations.claim: 'schemaDigests' occurs zero times in identity-model.py; the field is reached only by the generic annotation dispatch.
The whole enforced law for the raw-artifact representation is retention: blob(value).
An empty schemaDigests set admits.
Dropping the document a member Coverage was actually admitted under admits.
A registered document the view admitted nothing under admits.
An arbitrary retained blob admits as a member, contradicting the published registration sentence.
An unretained digest refuses; retention is the only real constraint.
The shipped reference producer over-lists: a view with zero relation facts still names relation-payload-schemas.v2.json, so the committed set is a strict superset of the mechanical union.
A committed view record in the live tree names a schemaDigests member whose bytes exist nowhere in the tree.
actualObservations.evidence: native/native-cases.v2.json fixtures.coverageView.schemaDigests[0] = 5665e5dd92cd022040142a63d8e183cc258f678baf8f0674f8da9ebe0302a7a4; exhaustive sha256 scan of the live tree found no matching file

actualObservations.claim: The adjacent site carries the same defect: an arbitrary retained blob is admitted as a domain='schema' evaluation input ref.

inferences.statement: The set is a deliberate producer declaration, not a derived union.

No floor (superset-of-union) obligation is required by the existing contract, because each fact and Coverage pins and retains its own schema document through its own payloadSchemaDigest, so schemaDigests carries no unique authority.
Two consumers selecting different schema sets from the same source repository is expected under the contract as written and is not evidence of divergent semantic inputs.

notProposed: Automatic maximal union of fact/coverage payload schemas — the existing contract does not require it and the reference producer contradicts it.
Any completeness floor on the declared set.
Blessing arbitrary unregistered documents or hidden evidence: the correction closes exactly that hole.

requiredExecutableCorrection.rationale: Two published statements (prose and field annotation) assert registration; the closure enforces retention only. Aligning the model is the minimal way to make the existing published law true without changing the selected-not-derived semantics.
requiredExecutableCorrection.approach: Annotation-driven, matching the contract's own rule that admission dispatches on the x-opensip-digest annotation and never on a field name.

changes.change: cached closed set of payload-registry documents by raw SHA-256 of exact full bytes, derived from x-opensip-payload-registry alone
after blob(value), refuse SCHEMA_DOCUMENT_UNREGISTERED:<digest> when artifactClass=='registered-schema-document' and the digest is not a registered document

proposedProse.text: `view.schemaDigests` is the producer's own **declaration** of the schema documents its view was produced under. Each member is the raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of a document on the closed registry above; a member naming anything else refuses (`SCHEMA_DOCUMENT_UNREGISTERED`). The set is **selected, not derived**: it is neither required to name every document a member fact or Coverage was admitted under, nor forbidden from naming a registered document this view admitted nothing under. It carries no admission authority of its own — every fact and Coverage pins its own document through its own `payloadSchemaDigest`, whose exact bytes are re-hashed and retained on every reference, so a document omitted here is still pinned there and a document added here admits nothing. The same rule holds wherever the `registered-schema-document` artifact class appears, including the `schema` proof-input-ref domain.

proposedSchemaAnnotation.artifact: the exact complete bytes of a schema document on the closed x-opensip-payload-registry list, DECLARED by this view's producer as a schema this view admitted under. The set is the producer's declaration and not a derived union: it is neither required to name every document a member fact or Coverage was admitted under, nor forbidden from naming a registered document this view admitted nothing under. Each member fact and Coverage independently pins and retains its own document through its own payloadSchemaDigest, which is where payload admission is decided.

implementerMustKnow: The set is chosen, not derived: there is no completeness obligation and no prohibition on naming a registered document this view admitted nothing under.
Every member must be a current registry document, exact full bytes, retained.
It grants no authority: never rely on it to establish what a view admitted, and never read omission as absence — payloadSchemaDigest is where that is decided.

advisories.title: Unpublished join between semantic-evidence.importIds and plan.importIds
advisories.severityBasis: The enforcement exists and is exact; only its statement is missing. No admitted Run is affected.

owningSelectors.existingRelatedProse: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md:191-197 (evaluated imports must belong to Plan; finding citation rules)

actualObservations.claim: close_run enforces evidence['importIds'] != plan['importIds'] -> IMPORT_JOIN.
Both arrays are uniqueItems with x-opensip-order 'canonical-set', enforced by ordered() (ORDER_OR_DUPLICATE), so list equality is canonical-set equality.
Evidence omitting a Plan-selected import refuses.
A Plan omitting an import the evidence names refuses.
A selected but non-evaluated import is lawful.
That non-evaluated selected import must still be retained.
An evaluated but unselected import refuses at its own distinct join.
A finding may cite an evaluated selected import.
A finding may NOT cite a selected-but-unevaluated import; selection alone grants no evidence authority.
The equality is stated in no published prose; the owning paragraph enumerates view and coverage root equalities and stops.
actualObservations.evidence: identity-and-evidence.md:505-506; no importIds occurrence in v2/contracts/product-v1 or v2/architecture prose

inferences.statement: This is a missing statement of an existing law, not a missing law.
Selection and evaluation are already cleanly separated: selection implies retention and admission, evaluation implies citability.

requiredExecutableCorrection.rationale: Control flow, schema and contract were verified directly; no mismatch exists. A synthetic join would add a second, weaker statement of a law the complete admitted Run already enforces.

notProposed: Any new join or model change.
Erasing non-evaluated selected imports from retention.
Adding imported facts implicitly to a view.

proposedProse.text: `semantic-evidence.importIds` repeats the Plan-selected import set **exactly**: the two are equal as canonical sets and any difference in either direction refuses (`IMPORT_JOIN`). It is a repetition of the Plan's selection, never a second selection — evidence can neither drop a selected import from the record nor add one the Plan did not select. `proof-bundle.evaluationInputRefs` separately names the subset actually **evaluated**, which must be a subset of the selected set (`UNSELECTED_EVALUATION_IMPORT`) and never grants authority to an unselected import. Selection is retention, not use: a selected import is resolved and admitted by the Run closure even when nothing evaluated it, and selection alone lets no finding cite it — import citations are restricted to the evaluated subset (`HIDDEN_FINDING_EVIDENCE`). A selected but non-evaluated import contributes no fact to any view.

proposedSchemaAnnotation.text: Exactly the Plan-selected import set of this Run's Plan, repeated: equal as a canonical set to plan.importIds (IMPORT_JOIN). A repetition of the selection, never a second selection. The evaluated SUBSET is named separately by proof-bundle.evaluationInputRefs; a selected import that nothing evaluated is still resolved and retained by the Run closure, and being selected alone grants it no evidence authority.
proposedSchemaAnnotation.digestConsequence: none — identity-schemas.v2.json is not a registered payload document, so no payloadSchemaDigest changes; its source-pins.v1.json row must be re-pinned
